jsonld.headline: Certificate of origin: which one you need and how to get it

acceptedAnswer.text: A preferential certificate is issued under a trade agreement and lets the buyer pay the lower agreement duty, if the goods meet its rules of origin. A non-preferential certificate only proves the goods are Indian and gives no duty cut.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between preferential and non-preferential certificates?

acceptedAnswer.text: On DGFT's Trade Connect platform, trade.gov.in, using your IEC-linked login. You choose the agreement and the issuing agency, fill in invoice and origin details, pay the fee and download a digitally signed eCoO.

mainEntity.name: Where do I apply for a certificate of origin in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Under India–UK CETA, the UK accepts an origin declaration completed by the exporter or producer. You can generate a self-declared eCoO on Trade Connect without a fee, with a DSC linked to your IEC. Keep the proof of origin for five years.

mainEntity.name: Can I self-certify origin for UK exports?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the agreement. Under India–UK CETA, a certificate or origin declaration is valid for 12 months from issue or completion. Check the deal page for other agreements.

mainEntity.name: How long is a certificate of origin valid?

acceptedAnswer.text: DGFT Appendix 2B lists agencies per agreement. The Export Inspection Council covers all goods, MPEDA covers marine products, and the Textiles Committee covers textiles and made-ups under most agreements.

mainEntity.name: Which agency issues preferential certificates?

jsonld.name: Apply on Trade Connect (eCoO)

step.text: Log in to trade.gov.in with your IEC-linked DGFT account. Keep your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign active in the profile.
Open Certificate of Origin and choose preferential or non-preferential, then the agreement and destination country.
Select the issuing agency: EIC, MPEDA or the Textiles Committee for preferential; a chamber or council for non-preferential.
Enter invoice details, the HS code and the origin criterion (wholly obtained, change of heading or value content), and upload the invoice plus cost sheet or input invoices where a value test applies.
Pay the agency fee online and submit. The agency may ask questions or inspect the goods.
Download the digitally signed eCoO with its QR code and send it to the buyer with the invoice before the goods arrive.

jsonld.headline: ECGC export credit insurance: cover against buyer default and country risk

acceptedAnswer.text: An exporter whose expected export turnover for the next year does not exceed ₹5 crore. ECGC describes it as suited to exporters with exposure of up to about ₹50 lakh on a single buyer. Exporters above ₹5 crore turnover use the Shipments Comprehensive Risks policy.

mainEntity.name: Who is eligible for the ECGC Small Exporters Policy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under the Small Exporters Policy, 95% of losses from commercial risks and 100% from political risks. Under the Shipments Comprehensive Risks policy, 90%. You must have declared the shipment, paid premium and held a valid credit limit on the buyer.

mainEntity.name: How much of my loss will ECGC pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single published rate. The premium depends on payment terms, credit period and the buyer's country classification. The Small Exporters Policy has a minimum premium of ₹5,000 for the policy period. Ask an ECGC branch for a quote on your buyers.

mainEntity.name: What does ECGC cover cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often not for that shipment, which is why LC-backed shipments can be excluded from the whole-turnover policies. ECGC can still cover the risk of the LC-opening bank failing to pay. It is most useful when you offer D/P, D/A or open account terms.

mainEntity.name: Do I need ECGC if I ship against a letter of credit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Within 360 days of the due date of the export bill, or 540 days from the expiry of the policy cover, whichever is earlier. Before that you must have reported the overdue bill on time and taken steps to recover the money.

mainEntity.name: When must I file an ECGC claim?

jsonld.name: How to make a claim

step.text: Declare every shipment monthly, by the 15th of the following month, and pay premium on time. Undeclared shipments are not covered.
Report overdue bills by the 15th of the next month once they cross the reporting limit (60 days past due under SEP, 30 days under SCR).
Act to reduce the loss. Follow up with the buyer, hold goods if possible, and take recovery steps, including legal action where advised.
File the claim within 360 days of the bill's due date or 540 days from policy expiry, whichever is earlier, with shipping documents, correspondence and proof of default.
Share recoveries. Money recovered from the buyer later is shared with ECGC in proportion to the loss each bore.

acceptedAnswer.text: FOB covers your costs until the goods are loaded on the vessel at the Indian port. CIF adds ocean freight and marine insurance to the buyer's named port. Under both terms, risk passes to the buyer once the goods are on board in India. Only the cost split differs.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between FOB and CIF price?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Exports are zero-rated. If you export under a Letter of Undertaking, you pay no IGST on the shipment and can claim a refund of input tax credit. Adding GST to a quote for a foreign buyer only makes your price look higher for no reason.

mainEntity.name: Should GST be added to my export price?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is safer not to. RoDTEP and drawback reach you only after the shipment, rates can be revised, and the benefit can be recovered if export proceeds are not realised in time. Price as if they were zero and treat them as extra margin.

mainEntity.name: Should I pass RoDTEP to the buyer as a discount?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed rule. It depends on how long you wait for payment and how volatile the currency has been. Many small exporters convert their rupee costs at a rate a little below today's rate. For large orders, a bank forward contract is the cleaner option.

mainEntity.name: How much FX buffer should I keep?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because that is what the goods actually cost them in their warehouse. A lower FOB price can still lose if your product attracts higher duty or freight than a competitor's. Knowing the landed cost also shows you when an FTA duty cut helps your offer.

mainEntity.name: Why does the buyer care about landed cost?

jsonld.name: Step by step: build your FOB price

step.text: Factory cost per unit. Raw material, labour, power, overheads and wastage. Use actual costs from your last three months, not a hopeful estimate.
Add your margin. Decide it before you talk to the buyer. First orders are small and fussy, so do not cut margin to zero to win them.
Add export packing and labelling. Export cartons, pallets, shrink wrap, fumigation for wooden pallets, buyer's labels and barcodes. These are often forgotten.
Add inland haulage. Truck or rail from your factory to the port or ICD, for example Moradabad to Mundra or Tiruppur to Tuticorin. Get a written quote from your forwarder.

Add CHA, port and terminal charges. Customs broker (CHA) fee, terminal handling charges (THC) at origin, documentation, seal and any examination charges. The total of steps 1 to 5 divided by quantity is your FOB price per unit.

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually your customs broker (CHA) files it electronically on ICEGATE using your IEC, GSTIN, invoice and packing list. You can file it yourself if registered, but most small exporters use a CHA. Check the draft checklist before filing, because errors delay refunds and incentives.

mainEntity.name: Who files the shipping bill?

acceptedAnswer.text: LEO is customs' permission for the goods to be loaded for export. It is granted after the shipping bill is assessed and any examination is complete. The LEO date is generally treated as the date of export for incentives and other purposes.

mainEntity.name: What is a Let Export Order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Customs links each shipping bill to your bank through the AD code registered at that port. Without it, export proceeds cannot be tracked against the shipment and incentive or refund credits can get stuck. It is done once per port or ICD.

mainEntity.name: Why do I need to register my AD code at the port?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your goods fill most of a 20-foot container, FCL is usually cheaper per unit and safer, with less handling. For a few pallets or cartons, LCL is more economical, but expect extra handling at the CFS and a few more days in transit.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose FCL or LCL for my first order?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Export General Manifest is filed by the shipping line or airline after departure, listing the cargo carried. Customs matches your shipping bill against the EGM before IGST refunds and drawback are processed, so a mismatch holds your money.

mainEntity.name: What is the EGM and why does it matter?

jsonld.name: Step by step: from booking to sailing

step.text: Book with a freight forwarder or shipping line. Give cargo details, HS code, volume, weight, port and target vessel. You get a booking confirmation with vessel, cut-off times and the empty-container pick-up point. Under FOB or FCA the buyer's forwarder may book instead.

Prepare documents. Commercial invoice and packing list, matching the order and any LC. Add a certificate of origin if the buyer wants FTA duty, and any inspection, phytosanitary or fumigation certificate your product needs.

Register your AD code at the port. Your bank's AD code and your bank account must be registered in the customs system at each port or ICD you export from. Without it, export proceeds and incentives cannot be linked to the shipping bill. You register it once per port on ICEGATE, with bank proof uploaded on e-SANCHIT, and customs at that port approves it; your CHA can help.

Stuff the container. Factory stuffing: the container comes to your premises, you load it, and it is sealed with an RFID e-seal under customs' self-sealing procedure. CFS stuffing: you truck cartons to a container freight station where they are packed, which is normal for LCL.

CHA files the shipping bill on ICEGATE. It carries your IEC, GSTIN, HS code, value, LUT or IGST details, drawback and RoDTEP claims, and the export declaration. Check the draft (checklist) carefully: errors here delay refunds and incentives.
Customs assessment and examination. The risk system decides whether goods are examined or cleared on documents. If selected, officers check the goods against the declaration.
Let Export Order (LEO). Once customs is satisfied it grants LEO. The goods can then be loaded. The LEO date is the date of export for most purposes.
Loading and bill of lading. After loading, the carrier issues the bill of lading (or air waybill). Check names, ports, description and the on-board date against your LC before accepting.
EGM. After sailing, the shipping line or agent files the Export General Manifest. Your shipping bill must match the EGM for IGST refunds and drawback to flow.

jsonld.name: How to export from India: step-by-step guide from IEC to e-BRC (2026) | Exportwalla
How to start exporting from India

step.name: Get your IEC
step.text: The Importer-Exporter Code is a 10-character number from DGFT, linked to your PAN. Apply on the DGFT website with a digital signature; the government fee is ₹500. Without an IEC you cannot file a shipping bill.

step.name: Register with your export promotion council (RCMC)
step.text: Each product family has a council: CLE for leather, AEPC for apparel, Spices Board, APEDA, EEPC, EPCH and others. The RCMC unlocks export incentives and buyer-seller meets.

step.name: Find your HS code
step.text: Every product has a 6-digit HS code used worldwide and an 8-digit ITC-HS code on Indian shipping bills. The code decides the duty your buyer pays, so get it right first.

step.name: Choose the country
step.text: Compare demand, growth, how much the country already buys from India and the duty on Indian goods. Trade agreements like India–UK CETA, India–UAE CEPA and India–Australia ECTA cut duty to zero on many lines.

step.name: Find genuine buyers
step.text: Start with importers who already buy your HS code. The UK publishes importer names (HMRC); elsewhere use Indian mission commerce wings, council fairs and verified shipment data. Never ship on open credit to a new buyer.

step.name: Price it: FOB, CIF and landed cost
step.text: Quote FOB (your price at the Indian port) and know the buyer's landed cost: freight, insurance, duty and import VAT. A lower duty from a trade deal is a selling point.

step.name: Prepare documents
step.text: Proforma and commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin for the trade deal, and product certificates. Preferential certificates are applied for on DGFT Trade Connect.

step.name: Ship and clear Indian customs
step.text: File a GST LUT to export without paying IGST, register your AD code at the port, and let your CHA file the shipping bill on ICEGATE.

step.name: Get paid and close out
step.text: Use advance payment, a letter of credit or ECGC cover. When the money arrives, the bank issues an e-BRC, which you need for RoDTEP, drawback and GST refunds.

acceptedAnswer.text: A Registration-cum-Allocation Certificate issued by APEDA after you upload your LC, contract or proforma invoice. Customs needs it with the export documents. For non-basmati rice it is valid for shipment within 45 days of issue.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an inspection certificate for rice to Europe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but the rice must come from a mill with ISO 22000 or HACCP, and before the RCAC is issued you must upload a certificate from the SFDA-accredited establishment you bought from.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Exporters of marine products must register with MPEDA, which DGFT lists as the body for marine products. The registration also serves as the RCMC you need for export benefits.

mainEntity.name: Is MPEDA registration compulsory for shrimp exporters?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. India is not certified under Section 609 of US law on sea-turtle protection, so only farmed shrimp is eligible. Every shrimp shipment, farmed or wild, must carry the DS-2031 declaration.

mainEntity.name: Can Indian wild-caught shrimp be exported to the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: As verified on 3 November 2026: company-specific anti-dumping and countervailing duties, plus a 10% Section 301 duty on Indian goods entered from 24 July 2026. Check USTR and Federal Register notices before quoting, as these change.

mainEntity.name: What extra US duties apply to Indian shrimp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The processing plant must be approved by EIC and appear on the EU list of approved establishments, and each consignment needs a health certificate. From 3 September 2026 the certificate also carries the EU antimicrobial-use attestation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need EIC approval to export shrimp to the EU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. The EU rules from 3 September 2026 cover how the shrimp was raised, so processors need records from hatcheries and farms showing no growth-promoting or reserved antimicrobials were used.

jsonld.headline: How to export spices from India

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Spices Board says a Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices (CRES) is mandatory in addition to the IEC for exporting spices. The CRES is also accepted in place of an RCMC, so you do not need a separate council membership for spices.

mainEntity.name: Is Spices Board registration compulsory?

acceptedAnswer.text: 5 µg/kg for aflatoxin B1 and 10 µg/kg for total aflatoxins. The same limits apply to ginger and nutmeg. The Spices Board tests export lots to the EU against these limits under its mandatory sampling and testing programme.

mainEntity.name: What is the EU aflatoxin limit for chilli and turmeric?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ethylene oxide was used to kill microbes in spices, but the EU does not allow it, and limits are set at very low levels. Since May 2024 the Spices Board has also required ethylene oxide testing for every spice consignment to Singapore and Hong Kong. Use steam sterilisation instead.

mainEntity.name: Why is ethylene oxide a problem for spice exports?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, for spices classified under HTS headings 0904 to 0910. The US notice that added 10% to most Indian goods from 24 July 2026 lists these headings in its exemption list (Annex II, Part A). Spice blends, sauces or extracts under other headings may not be covered, so check the exact US code with your importer's broker.

mainEntity.name: Do Indian spices pay the 10% US Section 301 duty?

acceptedAnswer.text: FDA does not approve facilities in advance, but the facility must be registered with the FDA and the registration renewed between 1 October and 31 December of each even-numbered year. FDA can detain shipments at the border for Salmonella or residues.

mainEntity.name: Does my spice unit need FDA approval to sell to the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not safely. EU pesticide limits apply to cumin, and the default limit for pesticides without a specific limit is 0.01 mg/kg. Test each lot before shipment and keep the report with the lot number on your documents.

jsonld.description: Find real overseas buyers: importers of your HS code, Indian mission commerce wings, EPC buyer-seller meets, trade fairs, and how to verify a buyer.
jsonld.headline: How to find export buyers: channels that work, and how to check a buyer

acceptedAnswer.text: Target companies that already import your HS code into your chosen market. They understand the product and the import process. The UK publishes importer names by commodity code through HMRC; for other countries, shipment data from private providers can give a starting list that you then verify.

mainEntity.name: What is the most reliable way to find export buyers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Indian missions abroad have commerce or trade sections that pass on trade enquiries, share importer contacts and support Indian participation in fairs. Write to the commercial officer with your product, HS code, capacity and certifications. Some enquiries are also posted on the Indian Trade Portal.

mainEntity.name: Can Indian embassies help me find buyers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Under the Export Promotion Mission, the Market Access Support intervention, which replaced the older Market Access Initiative scheme, funds trade fairs, buyer-seller meets and trade delegations, with airfare support for MSMEs at eligible events. Supported events change each year, so ask your EPC which ones are covered.

mainEntity.name: Is there government support for attending trade fairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can bring enquiries, but quality is mixed and scams are common. Never pay a fee to receive an order, verify every buyer in its company registry, and ask for advance or LC payment on any order that comes through a platform.

mainEntity.name: Are B2B platforms worth using?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the company registry, confirm they import your product, call their listed switchboard, ask for references, and keep the first order small with advance or a confirmed LC. Red flags include free email addresses, urgency and requests to change bank details.

mainEntity.name: How do I check that a foreign buyer is genuine?

jsonld.name: Channels, ranked by reliability

step.text: Importers who already buy your HS code. They know the product, the duty and the paperwork. In the UK, HMRC's uktradeinfo service lets you search traders by commodity code and publishes importer names and addresses (not values). For other markets, customs shipment data is sold by private providers; use it to list importers, then check them yourself. See exporting to the United Kingdom.

Commerce wings of Indian missions. Indian embassies and high commissions have commerce or trade sections that pass on trade enquiries, share importer lists and help at fairs. Write to the commercial officer with your product, HS code and capacity. Trade enquiries received by missions are also posted on the Indian Trade Portal.

Your export promotion council. EPCs run buyer-seller meets in India and abroad, reverse buyer-seller meets where buyers visit India, and India pavilions at trade fairs. These are mainly for member exporters with an RCMC.

International trade fairs. The best place to meet many buyers in a few days. The government's Export Promotion Mission now funds trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, reverse buyer-seller meets and trade delegations through its Market Access Support (MAS) intervention, which replaced the earlier Market Access Initiative (MAI) scheme, with airfare support for MSMEs at eligible events. Ask your EPC which events are supported this year.

B2B platforms. Useful for visibility, but full of price shoppers, fake buyers and scams. Never pay a fee to receive an order, and never ship on credit to a buyer who found you there. Treat a platform enquiry as a lead to verify, not as an order.

jsonld.description: Apply for an Importer-Exporter Code on the DGFT portal: who needs it, PAN link, documents, ₹500 fee, timeline and the April–June annual update.
jsonld.headline: How to get an IEC (Importer-Exporter Code) from DGFT

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Since July 2017 DGFT has used the PAN of the business as its IEC, and only one IEC can exist against one PAN. A proprietor's IEC is the owner's PAN; a company or LLP uses its own PAN. If you open a new company, it needs its own IEC.

mainEntity.name: Is the IEC number the same as my PAN?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It has no expiry date and no renewal fee. But you must update or confirm it online every year between April and June. If you skip this, DGFT can deactivate the IEC until you complete the update.

mainEntity.name: Does an IEC expire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The DGFT portal accepts Aadhaar-based e-sign as well as a Class 3 digital signature. For e-sign, the Aadhaar of the person signing must be linked to a mobile number that receives the OTP.

mainEntity.name: Can I apply without a digital signature?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If the merchant exporter buys from you in India and exports in its own name, its IEC goes on the shipping bill. You need your own IEC only when you export in your own name, which also lets you claim incentives and refunds directly.

mainEntity.name: I only sell to an exporter in India. Do I need an IEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Log in to the DGFT portal and complete the pending annual update. DGFT's fee schedule lists ₹200 for an update filed after the April–June window. Once it is submitted, the IEC is reactivated and customs and banks can use it again.

mainEntity.name: My IEC was deactivated. What now?

jsonld.name: Step by step: apply on the DGFT portal

step.text: Go to dgft.gov.in and register as an importer/exporter with your mobile number and email (OTP on both).
Log in and open the IEC application (form ANF-2A) under the IEC services menu.
Fill in the business name exactly as on PAN, the address, bank account, directors or partners, and any branch offices.
Upload the documents the portal asks for.
Pay the ₹500 fee online.
Sign the application with your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit.
Download the IEC certificate from the portal and save the login. You will need it every year.

itemListElement.name: HS code for export: find the right code

jsonld.description: How the HS code, India's 8-digit ITC-HS and the buyer's tariff line fit together, how to classify a product, and why the code sets your duty.
jsonld.headline: HS code for export: find the right code before you quote

acceptedAnswer.text: Only the first six digits. Every country that uses the Harmonized System shares the 6-digit code, then adds its own digits. India uses 8 digits, the UK and US use 10, and the EU uses 8 for its Combined Nomenclature and 10 for TARIC.

mainEntity.name: Is the HS code the same in every country?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 8-digit Indian tariff item (ITC-HS). The buyer's 10-digit code belongs on their import declaration, though you can also show it on the invoice to help them. The first six digits of both should match.

mainEntity.name: Which code goes on the Indian shipping bill?

acceptedAnswer.text: The customs authority of each country, using the General Rules of Interpretation. Your declaration is your responsibility in India; the importer is responsible abroad. A binding ruling removes the doubt.

mainEntity.name: Who decides the correct code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A UK importer with a GB EORI applies to HMRC for an Advance Tariff Ruling, generally valid three years. An EU importer applies for Binding Tariff Information, valid three years across the EU. Send them full product details and photos.

mainEntity.name: Can my buyer get a binding ruling in the UK or EU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Customs can reassess duty, recover incentives such as RoDTEP or drawback with interest, and levy penalties. Abroad, the buyer may lose the FTA rate and pay the full duty, which usually lands back on you as a claim.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I use the wrong code?

jsonld.name: How to classify, in plain words

step.text: Describe the product precisely: what it is made of, how it is made, what it does and how it is sold (single item, set, part).
Find the likely chapter, then read the four-digit heading text and the section and chapter notes. These are the law; chapter titles are only a guide (GRI 1).
An unfinished or unassembled article that already has the character of the finished one goes where the finished one goes (GRI 2).

If two headings fit, the more specific description wins. For mixtures and sets, the material or part that gives the essential character decides. If still tied, take the heading that comes last in number order (GRI 3).
If nothing fits, use the heading for the most similar goods (GRI 4). Normal packing and cases go with the goods (GRI 5).
Apply the same logic inside the heading to reach six digits, then pick India's eight-digit line (GRI 6).
Cross-check with India's tariff, the buyer's tariff and published rulings abroad.

jsonld.description: Incoterms 2020 for small Indian exporters: EXW, FCA, FOB, CFR, CIF, DAP and DDP, where risk and cost pass, and which term to pick for a first order.
jsonld.headline: Incoterms 2020 for Indian exporters: which term to quote and why

acceptedAnswer.text: FOB or FCA for most first orders, because your responsibility ends in India. CIF is fine for sea cargo if you have a firm freight and insurance quote. Avoid DDP until you know the buyer's market, since you would pay their import duty and tax.

mainEntity.name: Which Incoterm is best for a new Indian exporter?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Under CIF you pay freight and insurance to the destination port, but the risk passes to the buyer once the goods are loaded on board at the Indian port. If anything happens at sea, the buyer claims on the insurance policy you arranged.

mainEntity.name: Does CIF mean I am responsible until the goods reach the buyer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Incoterms 2020 requires at least Institute Cargo Clauses (C) cover, for at least 110% of the contract price, in the contract currency. The buyer can ask for wider cover, such as ICC (A), at their cost or in the agreed price.

mainEntity.name: What insurance must I buy under CIF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because with containers you hand the goods to the carrier at a terminal or ICD, before loading. Under FOB, the risk stays with you until the goods are on board, even though you no longer control them. FCA passes the risk at the handover point.

mainEntity.name: Why does ICC prefer FCA over FOB for containers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Incoterms deal with delivery, costs and risk. Payment, ownership and governing law must be written in your sales contract. Choose your payment method separately, such as advance, LC or collection.

mainEntity.name: Do Incoterms decide when I get paid?

jsonld.name: How to choose: a simple rule for a first order

step.text: Default to FOB or FCA if the buyer has a forwarder in India. You deliver locally and your risk ends early.
Offer CIF or CFR if the buyer wants a delivered-to-port price or you can get a good freight rate. Get a written freight and insurance quote before quoting.
Avoid EXW: as the Indian exporter you will still need to file the shipping bill to claim GST refund and incentives, so FCA at your factory is cleaner.

Avoid DDP until you know the market. You would pay import duty and VAT, may need a tax registration in the buyer's country, and carry customs delays that you cannot control. A wrong HS code or valuation becomes your cost.
Match your documents. The Incoterm on the invoice, contract, LC and insurance certificate must be identical. Mismatches are a common LC discrepancy.

jsonld.description: Export payment terms for Indian SMEs: advance, letter of credit, D/P, D/A, open account, risk for a new buyer, UCP 600, LC discrepancies and e-BRC.
jsonld.headline: Export payment terms: advance, letter of credit, collections and open account

acceptedAnswer.text: Full or part advance is safest. A confirmed letter of credit at sight is next, because a bank in India also promises to pay against compliant documents. Avoid D/A and open account with buyers you have not traded with before.

mainEntity.name: What is the safest payment term for a new export buyer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sight LC pays as soon as compliant documents are presented and checked. A usance LC pays after an agreed period, such as 90 days from the bill of lading date. You can often get the usance amount early by discounting it with your bank, at a cost.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between sight and usance LC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because of discrepancies: late shipment or presentation, invoice wording differing from the LC, a bill of lading without an on-board notation, amounts above the limit, or inconsistent names and ports. Under UCP 600 banks look only at documents, so small mismatches matter.

mainEntity.name: Why do banks refuse LC documents?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under RBI's 2026 export regulations, nine months from the date of shipment for goods, or twelve months if the export is invoiced or settled in rupees. Your bank can extend the period on request. Check with your AD bank, as RBI amended these limits during 2025 and 2026.

mainEntity.name: How long do I have to bring export money into India?

acceptedAnswer.text: An electronic Bank Realisation Certificate, generated on the DGFT portal against remittance data sent by your bank. It proves you were paid for the export. It is used to support incentive claims and refunds and to show FEMA compliance.

mainEntity.name: What is an e-BRC and why does it matter?

jsonld.name: FEMA rules: getting the money home on time

step.text: Route payment through your bank (AD bank). The shipping bill and export declaration feed into RBI's EDPMS, and your bank closes each entry when money arrives.

Realise within the time limit. The Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, in force from 1 October 2026, set nine months from the date of shipment for goods, or twelve months if invoiced or settled in rupees. Your bank can extend this on a reasoned request. For shipments made before 1 October 2026, ask your AD bank which period applies.

Unrealised bills have consequences. If payment stays outstanding more than one year past the due date (or any extension your bank allowed), you can export further only against full advance or an irrevocable LC. Drawback and RoDTEP can be recovered and IGST refunds paid back.
Generate e-BRC. Banks send inward remittance data to DGFT, and you generate the e-BRC on the DGFT portal against it. It is your proof of realisation for incentives and audits.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for every product. You can export most goods with only an IEC. But you need an RCMC to claim most Foreign Trade Policy benefits, and registration with APEDA, the Spices Board or MPEDA is compulsory before exporting their products.

mainEntity.name: Is RCMC compulsory for every exporter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Normally five years, counted from 1 April of the year it was issued to 31 March five years later, unless the council says otherwise. Renew it online on the DGFT e-RCMC service before it expires.

mainEntity.name: How long is an RCMC valid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brass artware, decorative metal items and other handicrafts come under the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH). Industrial brass parts and fittings are engineering goods and come under EEPC India.

mainEntity.name: Which council should a Moradabad brass exporter join?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each council sets its own registration fee and some add an annual subscription. APEDA, for example, charges ₹5,000 plus 18% GST for an RCMC valid five years. Check the fee on your council's page in the DGFT e-RCMC service before paying.

mainEntity.name: What does an RCMC cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If you export products from different families, for example garments and home textiles, you can register with each council. Use the RCMC that matches the product for which you claim a benefit.

mainEntity.name: Can I hold RCMCs from two councils?

jsonld.name: How to apply on DGFT e-RCMC

step.text: Get your IEC first. The RCMC is issued against it.
Log in to the DGFT portal with your IEC-linked account and open e-RCMC, then apply for a new RCMC.
Choose the registering authority (council or board), your products and whether you are a manufacturer or merchant exporter.
Fill in the details and upload what the council asks for: GST registration, manufacturing proof such as Udyam, factory licence or FSSAI, and bank details.
Pay the council's fee online. Each council sets its own fee and some also charge an annual membership subscription.
Sign with DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit. The council reviews it and issues an e-RCMC that you download from the portal.

jsonld.description: What RoDTEP and All Industry Rate drawback pay back, where the official rates are, how to claim on ICEGATE, and RoDTEP's status as of November 2026.
jsonld.headline: RoDTEP and duty drawback: what they pay and how to claim

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as a rule. Drawback refunds customs duty on inputs, while RoDTEP refunds other embedded taxes that are not refunded under any other scheme. Both are claimed in the same shipping bill, subject to each scheme's conditions.

mainEntity.name: Can I claim RoDTEP and drawback on the same shipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of November 2026, RoDTEP is notified only up to 31 December 2026 (DGFT Notification 41/2026-27). Whether it continues after that depends on a new notification. Check the RoDTEP page on dgft.gov.in before quoting for 2027 shipments.

mainEntity.name: Is RoDTEP available in 2027?

acceptedAnswer.text: In DGFT's Appendix 4R for exports from the Domestic Tariff Area, or Appendix 4RE for Advance Authorisation, SEZ and EOU exports, on the RoDTEP page of dgft.gov.in. Look up your exact 8-digit tariff item and any per-unit cap.

mainEntity.name: Where do I find the RoDTEP rate for my product?

acceptedAnswer.text: All Industry Rate drawback is paid in cash to the bank account you registered with customs at the port, after the let export order and the EGM. The shipping bill itself is the claim, so no separate application is needed.

mainEntity.name: How is drawback paid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use it to pay basic customs duty on your own imports, or transfer it on ICEGATE to another importer, usually at a small discount. A scrip transfers in full, and it lapses after its expiry date.

mainEntity.name: What can I do with a RoDTEP e-scrip?

jsonld.name: How to claim on ICEGATE

step.text: Register on ICEGATE with your IEC and DSC. Register your AD code and bank account at each port you ship from.
In the shipping bill, your customs broker enters the 8-digit tariff item, the drawback serial number and the RoDTEP claim for each item, with the declarations the schemes require.
After let export order and the EGM, drawback is processed and paid to your registered bank account.
For RoDTEP, a scroll is generated after the EGM. Create your RoDTEP credit ledger on ICEGATE and generate the e-scrip, signed with your DSC.
Use the e-scrip to pay basic customs duty on your own imports, or transfer it on ICEGATE to an importer who buys it. The whole balance of a scrip transfers at once.
Watch the expiry date shown in the ledger and use or sell the scrip before it lapses.

step.name: IEC banwaiye
step.text: IEC 10-character ka code hai jo DGFT deta hai, aapke PAN se juda hota hai. DGFT website par digital signature se apply karein; sarkari fees ₹500 hai. IEC ke bina shipping bill file nahi hota.

step.name: Apni export council se RCMC lijiye
step.text: Har product ki council hoti hai: leather ke liye CLE, kapde ke liye AEPC, masale ke liye Spices Board, aur APEDA, EEPC, EPCH. RCMC se incentives aur buyer-seller meets milte hain.

step.name: Apna HS code pata kijiye
step.text: Har product ka 6-digit HS code hota hai, aur shipping bill par 8-digit ITC-HS code lagta hai. Duty isi code se tay hoti hai, isliye pehle code sahi karein.

step.name: Desh chuniye
step.text: Demand, growth, wahan India se kitna mal jaata hai, aur Indian mal par duty dekhiye. India–UK CETA, India–UAE CEPA aur India–Australia ECTA jaise samjhauton se kai products par duty zero ho jaati hai.

step.name: Asli buyer dhundhiye
step.text: Unhi importers se shuru karein jo pehle se aapka HS code mangwate hain. UK importers ke naam HMRC publish karta hai; baaki deshon mein Indian embassy ka commerce wing, council fairs aur verified shipment data. Naye buyer ko udhaar par maal mat bhejiye.

step.name: Daam tay kijiye: FOB, CIF, landed cost
step.text: FOB yaani Indian port par aapka daam quote karein, aur buyer ka landed cost samjhiye: freight, insurance, duty aur VAT. Trade deal ki kam duty aapka selling point hai.

step.name: Documents taiyar kijiye
step.text: Proforma aur commercial invoice, packing list, trade deal ka certificate of origin, aur product certificates. Preferential certificate DGFT Trade Connect par apply hota hai.

step.name: Ship kijiye, Indian customs clear kijiye
step.text: GST LUT file karein taaki IGST bina export ho, port par AD code register karein, aur CHA ICEGATE par shipping bill file karega.

step.name: Payment lijiye aur refund claim kijiye
step.text: Advance, letter of credit ya ECGC cover use karein. Paisa aane par bank e-BRC deta hai, jo RoDTEP, drawback aur GST refund ke liye zaroori hai.

mainEntity.name: ECGC Small Exporters Policy kaun le sakta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small Exporters Policy mein commercial risk par 95% aur political risk par 100%. SCR policy mein 90%. Shart yeh hai ki shipment declare ki ho, premium diya ho aur buyer par valid credit limit ho.

mainEntity.name: ECGC nuksaan ka kitna hissa deta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ek fixed rate nahi hai. Premium payment terms, credit period aur buyer ke desh ki category par depend karta hai. SEP ka minimum premium ₹5,000 hai. Apne buyers ke liye ECGC branch se quote lein.

mainEntity.name: ECGC cover ka kharcha kitna hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Export bill ki due date se 360 din, ya policy cover khatam hone se 540 din, jo bhi pehle ho. Usse pehle overdue bill samay par report kiya ho aur recovery ke kadam uthaaye hon.

Overdue bill samay par report karein (SEP mein 60 din, SCR mein 30 din baad).
Nuksaan kam karne ke kadam uthaayein: buyer se follow-up, recovery, zaroorat ho to legal action.

Baad mein recover hua paisa ECGC ke saath share karein.

mainEntity.name: FOB aur CIF price mein kya farak hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi. Export zero-rated hai. LUT par aap bina IGST export karte hain aur input tax credit ka refund le sakte hain. GST jodne se aapka price bina wajah mehnga dikhega.

mainEntity.name: Kya export price mein GST jodna chahiye?

acceptedAnswer.text: Behtar hai na dein. RoDTEP aur drawback shipment ke baad milte hain, rate badal sakte hain, aur samay par payment na aane par wapas liye ja sakte hain. Inhe zero maan kar price banayein.

mainEntity.name: Kya RoDTEP buyer ko discount mein de dein?

acceptedAnswer.text: Koi fixed rule nahi hai. Yeh payment ke intezaar aur currency ke utaar-chadhaav par depend karta hai. Chhote exporter aksar aaj ke rate se thoda kam rate lete hain. Bade order par bank ka forward contract lein.

jsonld.name: Step by step: FOB price banayein

step.text: Factory cost per unit: raw material, labour, bijli, overheads aur wastage. Pichhle teen mahine ka asli cost lein.
Margin jodein: buyer se baat se pehle tay karein. Pehla order jeetne ke liye margin zero na karein.
Export packing aur labelling: cartons, pallets, wooden pallet ka fumigation, buyer ke labels aur barcodes.
Transport: factory se port ya ICD tak, jaise Moradabad se Mundra. Forwarder se likhit quote lein.
CHA, port aur THC: CHA fees, terminal handling, documents aur seal. Step 1 se 5 ka total, quantity se divide karein, yahi FOB per unit hai.

acceptedAnswer.text: Aam taur par aapka CHA ICEGATE par aapke IEC, GSTIN, invoice aur packing list se file karta hai. File karne se pehle checklist zaroor check karein, kyunki galti se refund aur incentive atakte hain.

mainEntity.name: Shipping bill kaun file karta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: LEO customs ki permission hai ki maal export ke liye load ho sakta hai. Yeh shipping bill assessment aur examination ke baad milta hai. LEO date ko aam taur par export ki date maana jaata hai.

mainEntity.name: Let Export Order kya hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Customs har shipping bill ko us port par registered AD code se aapke bank se jodta hai. Iske bina payment aur incentive link nahi hote. Yeh har port ya ICD par ek baar hota hai.

mainEntity.name: Port par AD code register kyon karna hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maal 20-foot container ka zyaadatar hissa bhar de to FCL per unit sasta aur surakshit hai. Kuchh cartons ya pallets ke liye LCL sasta hai, par CFS par handling aur kuchh din zyaada lagte hain.

mainEntity.name: Pehle order ke liye FCL ya LCL?

jsonld.name: Step by step: booking se sailing tak

step.text: Forwarder ya shipping line se booking. HS code, volume, weight, port aur vessel batayein. Booking confirmation mein vessel, cut-off aur khaali container ki jagah milti hai. FOB ya FCA mein buyer ka forwarder bhi book kar sakta hai.
Documents taiyaar karein. Invoice aur packing list order aur LC se match karein. FTA duty ke liye certificate of origin aur zaroori certificates jodein.

Port par AD code register karein. Bank ka AD code aur account har port ya ICD par customs system mein register hona chahiye, warna payment aur incentive shipping bill se link nahi honge. Yeh ICEGATE par har port ke liye ek baar hota hai, bank proof e-SANCHIT par upload karke, aur us port ka customs approve karta hai. CHA madad kar sakta hai.
Stuffing. Factory stuffing mein container aapke yahan bharta hai aur self-sealing procedure mein RFID e-seal lagti hai. CFS stuffing mein cartons CFS par bharte hain, LCL mein yahi hota hai.
CHA ICEGATE par shipping bill file karta hai jismein IEC, GSTIN, HS code, value, LUT, drawback aur RoDTEP claim hote hain. Checklist dhyaan se check karein.
Assessment aur examination. Risk system tay karta hai ki maal khulega ya sirf documents par clear hoga.
Let Export Order (LEO). Customs santusht hone par LEO deta hai, phir loading hoti hai.
Bill of lading. Load hone ke baad carrier B/L deta hai. Naam, port, description aur on-board date LC se milaayein.
EGM. Jahaz nikalne ke baad shipping line EGM file karti hai. Shipping bill aur EGM match hone par hi IGST refund aur drawback aate hain.

acceptedAnswer.text: Export zero-rated hai. LUT se bina IGST export karke bacha ITC wapas lein, ya IGST bhar kar refund lein. Dono mein tax export price mein nahi rehta.

mainEntity.name: Kya export par GST lagta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Har financial year ek baar, GST portal par form RFD-11 mein. 31 March ko khatam hota hai, isliye April mein pehle export invoice se pehle naya file karein.

mainEntity.name: LUT kitni baar file karna hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi. IGST bhar kar export kiye goods mein EGM aur sahi GSTR-3B ke baad shipping bill hi refund application hai. RFD-01 LUT wale ITC refund ke liye hai.

mainEntity.name: Kya goods ke IGST refund ke liye RFD-01 chahiye?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shipping bill aur GSTR-1 Table 6A ka invoice number alag hai. GSTR-1 galat ho to Table 9A se theek karein; shipping bill galat ho to port par customs officer se milein.

mainEntity.name: Refund par SB005 dikh raha hai, matlab?

jsonld.name: LUT (GST RFD-11) file karein

step.text: gst.gov.in par Services, User Services, Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT) kholein.
Financial year chunein; LUT 31 March ko khatam, isliye har April pehle export se pehle naya file karein.
Declarations tick karein, do gawahon ki details dein, DSC ya EVC se sign karein.
ARN note karein aur LUT reference har export invoice par likhein.

mainEntity.name: Export buyer dhoondhne ka sabse bharosemand tareeka kya hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan. Videsh mein Indian missions ke commerce ya trade section trade enquiries aage bhejte hain, importer contacts dete hain aur fair mein madad karte hain. Commercial officer ko product, HS code aur capacity ke saath likhein.

mainEntity.name: Kya Indian embassy buyer dhoondhne mein madad karti hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan. Export Promotion Mission ki Market Access Support scheme, jo purani MAI scheme ki jagah aayi hai, trade fair, buyer-seller meet aur trade delegation ke liye fund deti hai, aur MSMEs ko airfare support bhi. Har saal events badalte hain, EPC se poochhein.

mainEntity.name: Trade fair ke liye sarkari madad milti hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Company registry check karein, dekhein ki woh aapka product import karta hai, office number par call karein, reference maangein, aur pehla order chhota rakhein advance ya confirmed LC ke saath.

mainEntity.name: Buyer asli hai, kaise pata karein?

jsonld.name: Tareeke, bharose ke kram mein

step.text: Jo pehle se aapka HS code import karte hain. UK mein HMRC ki uktradeinfo site par commodity code se importer ke naam aur address milte hain (value nahi). Dekhein UK export page. Baaki deshon ke liye private shipment data se list banaayein aur khud check karein.
Indian mission ke commerce wing. Commercial officer ko product, HS code aur capacity likhkar bhejein. Missions ki trade enquiries Indian Trade Portal par bhi aati hain.
Aapki export promotion council. EPC buyer-seller meet, reverse buyer-seller meet aur trade fair mein India pavilion chalati hai, mukhya roop se RCMC wale member exporters ke liye.

International trade fair. EPC se poochhein is saal kaunse event hain.
B2B platform. Visibility milti hai par fake buyer aur scam bhi bahut hain. Order ke liye kabhi fee na dein.

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan. July 2017 se DGFT business ke PAN ko hi IEC maanta hai aur ek PAN par sirf ek IEC ho sakta hai. Nayi company banayi to uska alag IEC lagega.

mainEntity.name: Kya IEC number aur PAN ek hi hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi, koi expiry ya renewal fees nahi. Par har saal April–June mein online update ya confirm karna zaroori hai, warna DGFT IEC deactivate kar sakta hai.

mainEntity.name: Kya IEC expire hota hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Koi baat nahi. DGFT portal Class 3 DSC ke alawa Aadhaar e-sign bhi leta hai. Bas sign karne wale ka Aadhaar us mobile se juda hona chahiye jis par OTP aayega.

mainEntity.name: Digital signature nahi hai to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi. Agar merchant exporter apne naam se export karta hai to shipping bill par uska IEC lagega. Apne naam se export karna ho aur incentives seedhe lene hon tab apna IEC chahiye.

mainEntity.name: Main sirf India mein exporter ko maal bechta hoon. IEC chahiye?

acceptedAnswer.text: DGFT portal par login karke pending annual update poora karein. Window ke baad update ki fees DGFT list mein ₹200 hai. Update submit hote hi IEC phir active ho jata hai.

mainEntity.name: IEC deactivate ho gaya, ab kya karein?

jsonld.name: Step by step: DGFT portal par apply

step.text: dgft.gov.in par mobile aur email OTP se importer/exporter registration karein.
Login karke IEC services mein IEC application (form ANF-2A) kholein.
Naam bilkul PAN jaisa bharein, saath mein address, bank account, directors/partners aur branches.
Portal jo documents maange, upload karein.
₹500 fees online bharein.
DSC ya Aadhaar e-sign se sign karke submit karein.
IEC certificate download karein aur login sambhal kar rakhein, har saal kaam aayega.

acceptedAnswer.text: Sirf pehle 6 digit. Harmonized System use karne wale saare desh 6-digit code share karte hain, uske baad har desh apne digit jodta hai: India 8, UK aur US 10, EU 8 (CN) aur 10 (TARIC).

mainEntity.name: Kya HS code har desh mein same hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: India ka 8-digit tariff item (ITC-HS). Buyer ka 10-digit code unki import entry ke liye hai; invoice par madad ke liye likh sakte hain. Dono ke pehle 6 digit match hone chahiye.

mainEntity.name: Indian shipping bill par kaunsa code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Har desh ka customs, General Rules of Interpretation se. India mein declaration aapki zimmedari hai, bahar importer ki. Bade order se pehle binding ruling le lein, isse shak khatam ho jata hai.

mainEntity.name: Sahi code kaun tay karta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Customs duty dobara laga sakta hai, RoDTEP ya drawback interest ke saath wapas le sakta hai aur penalty laga sakta hai. Bahar buyer ka FTA rate chala jata hai aur claim aksar aap par aata hai.

mainEntity.name: Galat code lagaya to kya hoga?

jsonld.name: Code kaise chunein, aasaan bhasha mein

step.text: Product ko saaf likhein: kis cheez ka bana hai, kaise bana, kya kaam karta hai, kaise bikta hai.
Chapter dhoondh kar 4-digit heading ka text aur section/chapter notes padhein; yahi kanoon hai (GRI 1).
Adhura ya khula hua saman jo poore saman jaisa hai, usi heading mein jata hai (GRI 2).
Do heading fit hon to zyada specific wali; mixture ya set mein jo material asli pehchaan deta hai woh (GRI 3).
Kuch fit na ho to sabse milte-julte saman ki heading (GRI 4); normal packing saman ke saath (GRI 5).
Heading ke andar isi tarah 6 digit tak, phir India ki 8-digit line (GRI 6).

acceptedAnswer.text: Zyaadatar pehle order ke liye FOB ya FCA, kyunki aapki zimmedari India mein khatam ho jaati hai. Pakka freight aur insurance quote ho to CIF bhi theek hai. DDP se bachein.

mainEntity.name: Naye exporter ke liye kaunsa Incoterm sabse achha hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi. CIF mein freight aur insurance aap dete hain, par risk Indian port par jahaz par load hote hi buyer ka ho jaata hai. Raste mein nuksaan par buyer insurance claim karta hai.

mainEntity.name: Kya CIF mein maal pahunchne tak risk mera hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Incoterms 2020 ke hisaab se kam se kam Institute Cargo Clauses (C), contract price ke 110% par, contract ki currency mein. Buyer chahe to ICC (A) jaisa wider cover maang sakta hai.

mainEntity.name: CIF mein kaunsa insurance lena hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nahi. Incoterm sirf delivery, kharcha aur risk batata hai. Payment ka samay, ownership aur kanoon sales contract mein likhne hote hain. Payment method, jaise advance, LC ya collection, alag se chunein.

mainEntity.name: Kya Incoterm se payment ka samay tay hota hai?

jsonld.name: Pehle order ke liye simple niyam

step.text: Buyer ka forwarder India mein ho to FOB ya FCA dein.
Freight aur insurance ka likhit quote ho to CIF ya CFR dein.
EXW se bachein: GST refund aur incentives ke liye shipping bill aapko hi file karna hoga, isliye factory par FCA behtar hai.
DDP se bachein: buyer ke desh ki duty aur VAT aap par aayegi, wahan tax registration bhi lag sakta hai.
Invoice, contract, LC aur insurance par same Incoterm likhein. Price ke liye export pricing guide dekhein.

acceptedAnswer.text: Poora ya kuchh advance sabse surakshit hai. Uske baad confirmed sight LC, jismein India ka bank bhi sahi documents par payment ka vaada karta hai. Naye buyer ke saath D/A aur open account se bachein.

mainEntity.name: Naye buyer ke saath sabse surakshit payment term kaunsa hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discrepancy ki wajah se: late shipment, invoice ka description LC se alag, bill of lading par on-board notation nahi, amount limit se zyaada, ya naam aur port alag. UCP 600 mein bank sirf documents dekhta hai.

mainEntity.name: Bank LC documents kyon reject karta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: RBI ke 2026 niyamon mein goods ke liye shipment se nau mahine, rupee invoice par baarah mahine. Bank request par samay badha sakta hai. RBI ne 2025 aur 2026 mein yeh limit badli hai, isliye apne bank se confirm karein.

mainEntity.name: Export ka paisa India laane ke liye kitna samay hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Electronic Bank Realisation Certificate, jo aap DGFT portal par bank ke bheje remittance data se banate hain. Yeh saabit karta hai ki export ka paisa aa gaya. Incentive, refund aur FEMA compliance ke liye kaam aata hai.

mainEntity.name: e-BRC kya hai?

jsonld.name: FEMA: paisa samay par laayein

step.text: Payment apne AD bank se hi lein. Shipping bill RBI ke EDPMS mein jaata hai aur paisa aane par bank entry band karta hai.

RBI ke 2026 export regulations (1 October 2026 se lagu) mein goods ke liye shipment se nau mahine, rupee invoice par baarah mahine. Bank wajah dekhkar samay badha sakta hai. 1 October 2026 se pehle ki shipment ke liye apne AD bank se poochhein ki kaunsi muddat lagegi.

Paisa due date (ya bank ki di hui badhi muddat) ke ek saal baad bhi na aaye to aage sirf poore advance ya irrevocable LC par hi export kar sakte hain. Drawback, RoDTEP aur IGST refund bhi wapas dena pad sakta hai.
Paisa aane par bank DGFT ko data bhejta hai aur aap DGFT portal par e-BRC banate hain. Yeh paisa aane ka proof hai, jo incentive claim aur audit mein kaam aata hai.

acceptedAnswer.text: Har product ke liye nahi. Zyadatar maal sirf IEC se export ho jata hai. Par FTP benefits ke liye RCMC chahiye, aur APEDA, Spices Board ya MPEDA wale products mein registration pehle zaroori hai.

mainEntity.name: Kya har exporter ke liye RCMC zaroori hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aam taur par paanch saal, 1 April se paanch saal baad 31 March tak, jab tak council kuch aur na kahe. Expiry se pehle DGFT e-RCMC par renew karein.

mainEntity.name: RCMC kitne saal chalta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brass artware aur decorative metal items EPCH mein aate hain. Industrial brass parts aur fittings engineering goods hain, woh EEPC India mein aate hain. Dono bechte hain to dono councils ki RCMC le sakte hain.

mainEntity.name: Moradabad ka brass exporter kaunsi council join kare?

acceptedAnswer.text: Har council apni fees tay karti hai, kuch saalana subscription bhi leti hain. APEDA paanch saal ke RCMC ke ₹5,000 + 18% GST leta hai. Bharne se pehle DGFT e-RCMC par fees check karein.

mainEntity.name: RCMC ka kharcha kitna hai?

jsonld.name: DGFT e-RCMC par apply kaise karein

step.text: Pehle IEC lein.
DGFT portal par IEC wale account se login karke e-RCMC mein naya RCMC apply karein.
Council, products aur manufacturer ya merchant exporter chunein.
Details bharein aur council ke maange documents upload karein: GST, Udyam, factory licence ya FSSAI, bank details.
Council ki fees online bharein; kuch councils saalana subscription bhi leti hain.
DSC ya Aadhaar e-sign se submit karein; council check karke e-RCMC jaari karti hai.

jsonld.description: RoDTEP aur All Industry Rate drawback kya lautate hain, official rate kahan milte hain, ICEGATE par claim kaise karein aur November 2026 mein RoDTEP ki sthiti.
jsonld.headline: RoDTEP aur duty drawback: kya milta hai, kaise claim karein

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan, aam taur par. Drawback inputs ki customs duty lautata hai aur RoDTEP baaki chhupe taxes. Dono ek hi shipping bill mein claim hote hain, apni-apni shart ke saath.

mainEntity.name: Kya ek hi shipment par RoDTEP aur drawback dono mil sakte hain?

acceptedAnswer.text: November 2026 tak RoDTEP sirf 31 December 2026 tak notified hai. Aage naye notification par nirbhar hai. 2027 ke quote se pehle dgft.gov.in ka RoDTEP page dekhein.

mainEntity.name: Kya 2027 mein RoDTEP milega?

acceptedAnswer.text: dgft.gov.in ke RoDTEP page par Appendix 4R (DTA exports) ya 4RE (Advance Authorisation, SEZ, EOU) mein. Apna exact 8-digit tariff item aur uska per-unit cap dono dekhein.

mainEntity.name: RoDTEP rate kahan milega?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apne import ki basic customs duty bharein, ya ICEGATE par kisi importer ko bech dein. Poori scrip ek saath transfer hoti hai aur expiry ke baad lapse ho jati hai.

mainEntity.name: E-scrip ka kya karein?

jsonld.name: ICEGATE par claim kaise karein

step.text: IEC aur DSC se ICEGATE par registration; har port par AD code aur bank account register.
Shipping bill mein CHA har item ka 8-digit tariff item, drawback serial number aur RoDTEP claim bhare.

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan. Commercial export ke liye DGFT ka 10-character Importer-Exporter Code chahiye, jo aapke PAN se juda hota hai. Sarkari fees ₹500 hai aur online milta hai. Hamara desk file kar sakta hai.

mainEntity.name: Kya export ke liye IEC zaroori hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Set-up sasta hai: IEC fees, export council ki RCMC fees aur digital signature. Asli kharcha pehle order ka working capital hai, jo advance payment, letter of credit ya pre-shipment credit se cover hota hai. Yahan product check karna free hai.

mainEntity.name: Export shuru karne mein kitna paisa lagta hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yeh aapke HS code par depend karta hai. Hum 66 deshon ko aapke product ke liye market size, growth, India se kitna khareedte hain aur Indian maal par duty ke hisaab se score karte hain, aur top 5 wajah ke saath dikhate hain.

mainEntity.name: India se kaun sa product, kaun se desh mein bechein?

acceptedAnswer.text: Proforma aur commercial invoice, packing list, shipping bill (CHA ICEGATE par file karta hai), bill of lading ya airway bill, trade deal ka certificate of origin, aur product certificates. Payment ke baad bank e-BRC deta hai.

mainEntity.name: Export ke liye kya kya documents chahiye?

acceptedAnswer.text: UAE ke liye DGFT Trade Connect par apply kijiye; authorised agency CEPA certificate deti hai. UK ke liye exporter CETA origin declaration bharta hai, ya Indian issuing authority se certificate of origin leta hai. Data hum bhar dete hain.

mainEntity.name: UAE CEPA ya India–UK CETA ka certificate of origin kaise banaye?

acceptedAnswer.text: India–UK CETA 15 July 2026 se lagu hai aur Indian maal par kai lines par duty 0% ho gayi. Jaise leather footwear 8% se 0%. Apna HS code hamare UK page par dekhiye ya invoice upload kijiye.

mainEntity.name: India–UK FTA ke baad UK mein mere product par kitni duty hai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unhi importers se shuru kijiye jo pehle se aapka HS code mangwate hain: UK yeh HMRC ke zariye publish karta hai, baaki deshon mein desk shipment record check karta hai. Company registration check kijiye, naye buyer ko udhaar par maal mat bhejiye, aur bank details badalne ki baat phone par confirm kijiye.

mainEntity.name: Asli buyer kaise dhundhein aur fake buyer se kaise bachein?

acceptedAnswer.text: Advance payment, aapke bank se confirmed letter of credit, ya ECGC export credit insurance use kijiye. Ship karne se pehle desk LC documents check karta hai taaki bank mana na kare.

mainEntity.name: Payment kaise milega, aur buyer na de to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Importer apne desh mein duty aur import VAT deta hai. Aap FOB (Indian port par daam) ya CIF (freight aur insurance ke saath) quote karte hain. Zyadatar desh CIF par duty lagate hain; US, Canada, Australia aur New Zealand FOB par.

mainEntity.name: Customs duty kaun deta hai, exporter ya importer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan, zyadatar maal ke liye. Letter of Undertaking (LUT) file kijiye taaki IGST diye bina export ho, ya IGST dekar refund claim kijiye.

mainEntity.name: Kya export ke liye GST registration chahiye?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan, export incentives aur buyer-seller meets ke liye. Yeh aapke product ki export promotion council se milta hai, jaise leather ke liye CLE, kapde ke liye AEPC, masale ke liye Spices Board, ya EEPC.

mainEntity.name: Kya RCMC chahiye, aur kis council se?

acceptedAnswer.text: Haan. Apne IEC, buyer aur refund ke saath exporter aap hi rahenge. Tools free hain; export desk ki fees har shipment par, ₹12,000 plus GST se shuru, koi subscription nahi.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Commercial exports need the 10-character Importer-Exporter Code from DGFT, linked to your PAN. The government fee is ₹500 and it is issued online. Our desk can file it for you.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an IEC to export from India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Set-up is cheap: the IEC fee, your export council's RCMC fee and a digital signature. The real cost is working capital for the first order, which advance payment, a letter of credit or pre-shipment credit can cover. Checking your product here is free.

mainEntity.name: How much money do I need to start exporting?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your HS code. We score 66 countries for your product on market size, growth, how much they already buy from India and the duty they charge on Indian goods, and show the top five with the reason for each.

mainEntity.name: Which product and which country are best for export from India?

acceptedAnswer.text: A proforma and commercial invoice, packing list, shipping bill (filed by your CHA on ICEGATE), bill of lading or airway bill, the certificate of origin your trade deal needs, and any product certificate. After payment the bank issues the e-BRC.

mainEntity.name: What documents are needed to export?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the UAE, apply on DGFT Trade Connect and an authorised agency issues the CEPA certificate. For the UK, the exporter completes the CETA origin declaration, or gets a certificate of origin from an Indian issuing authority. We pre-fill the data for you.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a certificate of origin for UAE CEPA or the India–UK CETA?

acceptedAnswer.text: The India–UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026 and cut duty to 0% on many lines for Indian goods. Leather footwear, for example, went from 8% to 0%. Check your exact HS code on our UK page or upload an invoice.

mainEntity.name: What is the UK import duty on my product after the India–UK FTA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with importers who already import your HS code: the UK publishes them through HMRC, and our desk verifies shipment records elsewhere. Check the company registration, never ship on open credit to a new buyer, and confirm any change of bank details by phone.

mainEntity.name: How do I find genuine buyers and avoid fake ones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use advance payment, a letter of credit confirmed by your bank, or ECGC export credit insurance. Our desk checks LC documents before you ship so the bank does not refuse them.

mainEntity.name: How will I get paid, and what if the buyer does not pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: The importer pays duty and import VAT in their country. You quote FOB (your price at the Indian port) or CIF (including freight and insurance). Most countries charge duty on CIF; the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand charge it on an FOB-based value.

mainEntity.name: Who pays the customs duty: the exporter or the importer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most goods. File a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) to export without paying IGST, or pay IGST and claim the refund.

mainEntity.name: Do I need GST registration to export?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, to claim export incentives and join buyer-seller meets. It comes from the export promotion council for your product, for example CLE for leather, AEPC for apparel, the Spices Board or EEPC.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an RCMC, and from which council?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You stay the exporter of record with your own IEC, buyer and refunds. The self-serve tools are free; the export desk charges per shipment, from ₹12,000 plus GST, with no subscription.

acceptedAnswer.text: The Harmonized System code is a 6-digit number that classifies a product the same way in about 200 countries. India adds two digits (ITC-HS) for the shipping bill, and the buyer's country adds its own digits for its tariff.

mainEntity.name: What is an HS code?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is a search over the official tariff descriptions, not a customs ruling. Check the description against your product, and if two codes look possible, ask your CHA or our desk. A wrong code means the wrong duty.

mainEntity.name: Is the code from this tool final?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 8-digit ITC-HS code on Indian export documents. Its first six digits are the HS code this tool finds. If your old invoices already carry a code, use that.

mainEntity.name: Which code goes on my invoice?

acceptedAnswer.text: It decides the duty your buyer pays, whether a trade deal applies, which product rules and tests apply, and which export incentives (RoDTEP, drawback) you can claim. See HS codes for export.

acceptedAnswer.text: Import duty is paid by the buyer (or whoever imports the goods) in the destination country. It still decides whether your price works, so know it before you quote.

mainEntity.name: Whose duty is this?

acceptedAnswer.text: The normal (MFN) rate applies to goods from any WTO member. A trade deal like India–UK CETA or India–UAE CEPA gives Indian goods a lower rate if you send the right proof of origin. See certificate of origin.

mainEntity.name: Why are there two rates?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the UK and the US it is the national tariff line. For other countries it is the average of that country's lines inside the 6-digit code, from WTO/UNCTAD data via the World Bank; your exact line can differ. Each result links to its source.

mainEntity.name: How exact is the rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Most countries also charge VAT or GST on the value plus duty, which the importer usually reclaims. Use the export price calculator for the full landed cost.
